doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Faith and music as a ministry
summary: Bennett says he has been a Christian since youth and sees playing as a gift and service to audiences.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: You’re very thoughtful about — are you a man of faith? Yes. And how does it help you in your day to day dealings?

Well you know I think I’ve been a Christian since I was very young. I didn’t understand it but looking back I think that the light bulb probably went off for me at an early age. Well number one I realized that I had been given a gift, which I’m very grateful for. It’s not my own doing, you know, I received a gift. I work my hardest at it to cultivate it and do the best I can. And where this plays in for my own peace of mind is if I can keep my mind in that sense that what I’m doing is a service — not to sound pious or anything, I’m just being real. In a sense it’s a ministry because if I can go out there and play for people and give them some joy then that’s why we do this. So then it becomes less about me. Because I think anybody who’s an artist or a musician, sometimes we get to grow too far inward, where we’re looking at ourselves and gee I hope I can do this perfectly or I can keep improving, you know me, me, me. And that can be really defeating. So it’s a good — I’m just trying to balance working really hard with all my might at this that I’ve been given, but this is apparently what I’ve been put on earth to do so if I can do that to the best of my ability then I’m happy. You know?
